title: LLS Monitoring Export v1 — batch request body
description:
Request body for POST /api/v1/monitoring/export.

A batch is a transport convenience, nothing more. It has no transactional meaning: each envelope is accepted, quarantined, rejected or failed on its own, and the acknowledgement reports every one individually. A publisher must never infer the fate of one message from the fate of its neighbours, and must never delete a batch from its outbound queue on the strength of an HTTP 200 alone.

schema_version.description: Version of the batch wrapper. Each envelope carries its own schema_version; a batch may legitimately mix minor versions.

batch_id.description: Optional transport-level identity, useful for tracing a retry through logs. NOT an idempotency key — idempotency is per message_id, and the same message may legitimately arrive in two differently-identified batches.

source_id.description: Must match the scope of the presented credential, and must match every envelope's source_id in this batch.

sent_at.description: When the publisher put this batch on the wire. Compared against receipt time to expose transport delay separately from generation delay.

queue_depth.description: Publisher's own outbound backlog at send time. Surfaced on the dashboard's transport-health view so a growing backlog on the LLS side is visible here before data goes missing.

messages.description: Envelopes, in any order. The receiver does not assume arrival order matches source order and orders by (source_instance, sequence) and the qualified timestamps instead.
